main_text.p: Plato, ἀεὶ μὲν δὴ τὴν φύσιν τῆς Γλαύκωνος ἠγασάμην, ἀπὰρ οὔω ἡ τότε πάνυ γε ἤσθην, femper quidem naturam Glauconis admiratus fum, fed præcipuè tum ea fum delectatus. ἀντὰρ aft: Homer. ἀντὰρ ἐγώ, aft ego. Sic μὲν, ὅμως, tamen.

Disjunctiva: ἢ νύξ, ἢ ἡμέρα, aut nox, aut dies: ἦτοι ἀγαθὸν, ἢ φαῦλον, aut bonū, aut malum. Aliquando ἢ distinguendo interrogat: Demosthenes, πότερον πάντα ταῦτα ποιῶν ἡσύχει ἢ παρεσκευάζει ἢ εἰρήνην, ἢ ὄ; utrúmne omnia hæc faciens injuriabatur, & fœdera violabat, & solvebat pacem, an non?
Caufalis: γάρ. Æschylus, σὺ γὰρ αὐ κλῆμα ἔπισκήψας; tu enim vicum ad defectionem solicitasses?

page.notes: Greek accents and the Greek passages are reproduced as far as legible; some Greek words in the Disjunctiva and Demosthenes passages are doubtful. Small specks on the page are stains, not text.
